open_points.subject: M02 Slot / action "author a function contract or implementation"
open_points.text: "`purpose`: plain words for the owner and the agent, fixed when the slot is created;" + "created when an agent with the author right issues the first contract version under a new slot name — there is no separate create action."
open_points.question: When the first contract for a new slot name is authored, how is `purpose` provided and validated, and what happens if later requests provide a different purpose (or none)?
options: `purpose` is mandatory only on first contract of a new slot; later requests must omit it
`purpose` is optional on first contract with a default (e.g., empty)
`purpose` is supplied on every author request but must match the stored one after creation
open_points.default_guess: Require `purpose` on first contract creation, store it immutably, and reject any later mismatch.

open_points.subject: M12 Flow / action "compose and prove a flow"
open_points.text: "The named place of a flow whose versions change..." + "`purpose` of a flow is fixed when the flow is created;" + "the first flow version composed under a new name creates the flow — there is no separate create action;"
open_points.question: When composing the first version of a new flow name, how is flow `purpose` set, and what is the rule if subsequent compositions include a different purpose (or omit it)?
options: `purpose` required only for first version of a new flow
`purpose` optional with default at flow creation
`purpose` always present in compose input but immutable once created
open_points.default_guess: Require `purpose` on first version creation and reject changes afterward.

open_points.subject: M10 ManifestOperation vs K-16 installation facts
open_points.text: M10: "each is absent when the installation selects no instance..." versus K-16: "An installation selects one manifest instance per service".
open_points.question: Can an installation legally have no selected instance for a service that appears in kernel operations, or must exactly one instance always be selected?
options: Exactly one instance per service is always required
Some services may have no selected instance, and operations for them are unavailable/refused
open_points.default_guess: Treat missing instance as invalid configuration because K-16 says one selected instance per service.

open_points.subject: M22 SpooledFile reader action surface
open_points.text: M22: "Read by ... the owner's approval preview and `read_spooled_file`" versus K-11: "The kernel exposes one fixed set of typed operations over `mcp`: inspect, author, try, run, resume, read traces, and the owner's approve, accept, activate, grant, revoke, resolve and cancel."
open_points.question: Is `read_spooled_file` a product action on the MCP surface or not? If not, through which listed action are spooled file bytes read?
options: `read_spooled_file` is an additional MCP action and K-11/action list must include it
No separate action exists; only metadata is readable and bytes are never directly returned
Byte access is embedded inside an existing listed action (must be named explicitly)
open_points.default_guess: Assume no separate action and expose only spooled-file metadata unless another listed action is explicitly defined to stream bytes.
